label: late original-phase x/u/n/1/h/q/v/f input after several t/c/j/k/e-type tokens
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, at positions 3-8, and never on the delimiter or during copying. The firing rate goes up with position (0.7% at t=3, 8.8% at t=8) and with L. It is driven by the current input token: x is strongest (27% of activation mass), followed by u, n, 1 and h, with q, v and f weaker. It is near-silent on p and d and on most other tokens. It is gated by the earlier context: it is much more likely when several earlier inputs come from {t,c,j,k,e,w,o,z,y,0,r,i,l}. A first token of t gives 4.6x lift, and the top examples nearly all start with t. It favours first occurrences of the input token. The input-token gate alone reaches mass recall 0.90 but precision only 0.17. Adding the context count raises F1 only to about 0.42, so the dependence on earlier tokens looks like a distributed hidden-state direction that this predicate approximates crudely.
